preds: In **Jordan**, the Press and Publications Law was amended yesterday in a way that restricts the right to freedom of expression on the Internet.
At the same time, journalists and advocates of free speech held a peaceful demonstration in front of the parliament where the law was being approved.
Internet freedom advocates holding a banner that read “Internet Freedom” as a leading slogan pointed out the trend toward the death of the internet in Jordan.
The protesters wore black clothes for this proclamation, which was called the “burial of the internet.

The approved law is still awaiting implementation; it requires the approval of the upper parliament and the signature of King Abdullah II, which is required before any laws come into effect in Jordan.
Jemil Nimeri, a member of parliament who opposed the proclamation, not only opposed the proclamation but also took part in the protest.
According to what he said, such proclamations serve only to suppress the voices of the people by restricting freedom.
Website owners are held responsible even for the comments that their readers post on their websites.
The draft proclamation sparked strong opposition, and it immediately triggered an online movement aimed at drawing attention to the controversy it was causing among netizens.
On Twitter, netizens have expressed their frustration in writing.
